questions.explanation: A finished time in the past ('yesterday') uses the past simple.
A past action with a present result uses the present perfect.
questions.q: I ___ my keys. I can't find them.

questions.explanation: A finished past period uses the past simple.
'Since 2019' connects past to now: present perfect.
'Last week' is finished time: past simple.
No past time is mentioned, and the experience matters now: present perfect.
questions.q: We ___ that film. It was great!

questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' needs the past simple: 'saw'.
A past action with a present result uses the present perfect.
questions.q: He ___ his leg. He's in hospital now.

questions.explanation: 'In 2022' is finished time: past simple.
Life experiences with no finished time use the present perfect.
'Two hours ago' is finished time: past simple.
A past action with a present result uses the present perfect.
questions.q: I ___ breakfast, so I'm not hungry.

questions.explanation: 'In 2020' is finished time, so use the past simple: 'visited'.
options: He went home an hour ago.
They saw that film last night.

questions.explanation: 'How long' with 'still now' uses the present perfect.
'Since Monday' connects past to now: present perfect negative.
'An hour ago' is finished time: past simple.
questions.q: She ___ her homework an hour ago.

questions.explanation: 'Just' with a recent action uses the present perfect.
After 'Did' use the base verb.
Life experiences use 'Have you ever' + past participle.
'For ten years' up to now uses the present perfect.
questions.q: We ___ each other for ten years.
